messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] sev=P2 prefill OOM spike detected (10+ errors/min) on pool=gpu-preload region=us-west-2 node=gpu-07 container=redwood-runtime-7f9a
maya: seeing repeated container restarts, likely OOM during prefill for long-context requests
sam: paging oncall @oncall-sre
oncall-sre: taking it. what's the visible customer impact?
maya: ~12% of large-context requests to model=rw-medium failing mid-prefill; streaming connections dropping. A couple enterprise customers hitting timeouts.
raj: grabbing logs now. snippet:
```
[2026-03-16T22:14:02Z] runtime error: CUDA out of memory at /workspace/inference/alloc.cu:421
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
[signal 6]
Container restarted (exit code 6)
```
lee: `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide | grep redwood-runtime` -> 5 replicas, 3 on gpu-07 showing RESTARTS 4-7 in last 10m
maya: hypothesis: very long prefill + aggressive batch prefetch + KV cache growth -> OOM and kernel-level fragmentation on older A100s
sam: short-term mitigation suggestions?
maya: 1) drain node gpu-07 to stop noisy restarts and protect other pods
2) enable model-fallback to smaller quantized variant for requests with large-context hints
3) reduce prefill_max_tokens (trim prefixes) via runtime config and roll restart
raj: adding: temp throttle of concurrent prefill ondedicated pool, increase failure budget so router sends to fallback
oncall-sre: initiating drain: `kubectl drain gpu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`
oncall-sre: cordon set, pods being evicted (will take ~90s)
maya: rolling config patch: `kubectl patch cm runtime-config -n inference -p '{"data":{"prefill_max_tokens":"4096"}}'` and then `kubectl rollout restart ds/redwood-runtime`
raj: applied patch, rolling restart started. also toggled `enable_fallback_long_context=true` in routing table for customers with context>8k
customer-success: notifying affected customers (acme-analytics, bigchat.ai) with an interim note about degraded experience; prepping follow-up message
sam: monitoring metrics: prefill OOM traces dropped to 0 on gpu-07 after drain + restart, container restarts reduced to 0 in last 5m
lee: quick kernel dmesg from gpu-07 saved to S3: s3://redwood-ops/logs/gpu-07-dmesg-8790012345.log
maya: root-cause (working theory): mem fragmentation + large single allocation patterns during prefill (long prompts) interacting with driver 520.x on older cards. will schedule driver bump and quiet configuration changes
raj: action items captured: [1] schedule driver update on gpu-07 and similar hosts, [2] add per-tenant prefill guardrails, [3] add alert rule: pager when restart_rate>1/min for >=3min, [4] populate runbook section for prefill-ooms
oncall-sre: handoff: leaving to afternoon oncall. marked node cordoned and remediation tickets created: INF-3421, INF-3422
customer-success: sent proactive customer note and will follow up with post-incident update once root cause confirmed
maya: post-mitigation: system stable, no new OOMs observed for 18m. will keep monitoring for 2 hours then close incident
sam: thanks all — capturing notes in incident doc and adding the dmesg + trace links.
maya: :white_check_mark: closing thread once oncall confirms no recurrence
